# Use-Case Model — Carcassonne (MODERNIZED)

* **Source:** `output/Carcassonne` (legacy code at pinned commit `ca2797745a863243fa6ce96af63435b0d67bf2ab`)
* **Modernization plan:** `modernization-plan.json` (decisions M-1, M-2, M-3, M-4, M-5; directives D-1, D-2)
* **Generated by:** the modernize-modeler skill from the codebase-modeler output.
Legacy citations `path:line` point at the pre-modernization code; `Artifact.md:line`
citations point at the source artifact; `(M-n)` references the modernization plan.

This document is the modernized use-case model for the **Carcassonne** multiplayer
browser game. It preserves the legacy business use cases, UC ids (UC-01…UC-08), actors,
and pre/post-conditions (kept elements K-1, K-3, K-4, K-5, K-6) and rewrites the technical
plumbing to the most modern JavaScript/TypeScript stack: a TypeScript/React 19 single-page
client (M-1), a Node.js 24 + `ws` 8.x server owning the single authoritative game state
(M-2), a typed WebSocket JSON protocol (M-3), server-side move/turn revalidation (M-4), and
structured error/rejection payloads (M-5). Companion artifacts: [./Specification.md](./Specification.md),
`ActivityDiagram.md`, `ClassModel.md`, `DatabaseModel.md`, `DomainModel.md`.

---

## 1. Introduction

### 1.1 Purpose

To capture the functional requirements of the **Carcassonne** multiplayer browser game and
describe how players interact with the modernized system: lobby registration and management,
game start, the tile/meeple turn loop, majority scoring, and reconnection to an in-progress
game — now implemented end-to-end through a typed WebSocket JSON protocol (M-3) between a
TypeScript/React 19 single-page client (M-1) and a Node.js 24 + `ws` 8.x server that owns the
single authoritative in-memory state (M-2), revalidates every move server-side (M-4), and
returns structured rejections for failures (M-5). The use-case identities, ids, and
business-level pre/post-conditions are carried over unchanged from the legacy model (K-1,
K-3, K-4, K-5, K-6); each modernization is traceable to a plan decision.

### 1.2 Scope

**In scope:** the 8 lobby/game use cases (UC-01…UC-08) driven through the typed WebSocket
JSON protocol (M-3). The modernized code is a TypeScript full stack: a React 19 single-page
client with `RegistrationView`, `LobbyView`, and `GameBoard` components (M-1), a Node.js 24
+ `ws` 8.x server owning one authoritative in-memory state (lobby | game) (M-2), and a pure
TypeScript domain core ported 1:1 from the legacy game rules (K-1).

**Out of scope:** the Terminate Game feature (kept in the rewrite but not modeled as one of
the 8 UCs — see Resolved Assumptions & Issues, A-39), tile asset data, and debug-mode
internals (the debug SideId overlay stays a non-interactive visual layer, K-5).

## 2. System Boundary & Actors

The system boundary is the typed WebSocket JSON protocol (M-3): clients send the 8
client→server messages, and the game server (Node.js 24 + `ws` 8.x, M-2) replies via a
targeted send or a broadcast of the 8 legacy server→client messages (10 including the two M-5 additions). In the legacy system this
boundary was the Lamdera `ToBackend`/`ToFrontend` ADT surface in `src/Types.elm`
(`src/Types.elm:50-58`, `src/Types.elm:67-86`); the message identities and state-gating are
preserved (K-6) while the transport becomes typed JSON validated with zod before dispatch
(M-3), and every full-state reply is broadcast to all connected clients including the acting
one (M-3). The protocol also gains two typed rejection messages (M-5) that had no legacy
counterpart.

### 2.1 Primary Actors

* **Player (browser)** (*UC-A1*, human): A human player operating the modernized client — a
TypeScript/React 19 single-page app (M-1) that renders `RegistrationView`, `LobbyView`, and
`GameBoard` (K-5) and holds client state in a reducer fed by typed WebSocket updates (M-1).
There is **no host/admin role** (K-3): every name in the lobby gets a kick control, every
lobby client gets the Start button, and the "Kill lobby" button is situational (rendered only
for the full-lobby client, K-5). The backend now binds each WebSocket session to the
registered player and revalidates turn ownership server-side (M-4). Single role: `PLAYER`.
(legacy `src/Views/PlayerLobbyView.elm:30-37`, `src/Views/PlayerLobbyView.elm:20-23`,
`src/Backend.elm:125-133`) — kept (K-3); frontend modernized (M-1); turn ownership now
server-enforced (M-4).

### 2.2 Secondary / System Actors

* **Game server (Node.js 24 + `ws` 8.x)** (*UC-A2*, system): The self-hosted server process
that owns the single authoritative in-memory state (lobby phase | game phase, K-4). It
delivers typed client→server messages (M-3), broadcasts full-state updates to all connected
clients including the acting one (M-3), runs the in-process Fisher–Yates shuffle (M-2),
revalidates move legality and turn ownership before applying any move (M-4), and returns
structured rejections (M-5). It replaces the legacy **Lamdera platform** secondary actor
(M-2). (legacy `src/Backend.elm:6`, `src/Backend.elm:189-191`) — replaced (M-2).

**Diagram Description:** The **Player (browser)** is the only primary actor, operating the
modernized React 19 client (M-1); every use case is initiated by a player action (a name
entry, a lobby control, a board/tile/meeple click). The **Game server (Node.js 24 + `ws`
8.x)** is the secondary/system actor that replaces the legacy Lamdera platform (M-2): it owns
the single authoritative state (K-4), revalidates the move-bearing use cases server-side
(M-4), and fans out full-state broadcasts to every connected client including the acting one
(M-3), so dashed associations mark its supporting role. All eight use cases sit inside the
system boundary, which is now the typed WebSocket JSON protocol (M-3); UC-07 is system-internal
(no player action of its own — it is triggered by UC-06 or by draw-stack exhaustion, A-44).

## 4. Use-Case Specifications

### UC-01: Register a player in the lobby

**1. Brief Description**
Player submits a name in the registration view; the client trims it locally and sends
`RegisterPlayer` over the typed WebSocket protocol (M-3); the server (M-2) deduplicates,
enforces the 5-player limit (K-3), and broadcasts `PlayerRegistrationUpdated` to every client
(M-3). A duplicate name or a full lobby now returns a structured `RegistrationRejected {
reason }` (M-5) instead of a silent drop.

**2. Actors**
* **Primary:** Player (browser) (UC-A1)
* **Secondary:** Game server (UC-A2) (M-2)

**3. Pre-conditions**
* *Server:* The server is in the lobby phase (`BePlayerRegistration`). `src/Types.elm:11-14`, `src/Backend.elm:28-34` — kept (K-3)
* *Client:* The player's browser holds an open WebSocket connection to the game server (M-3). (was: connection subscription registered. `src/Backend.elm:189-191`) — M-3

**4. Post-conditions**
* *System State:* The new name is in the lobby list (when accepted) and every client received `PlayerRegistrationUpdated`. `src/Backend.elm:110-113` — kept (K-4)
* *System State:* The registering client moved from the registration view to the lobby view. `src/Frontend.elm:60-61` — kept (K-5)

**5. Main Success Scenario (Happy Path)**

| # | Lane | Step | Code Reference | Modernization |
| :- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | **Actor** | Player types a name into the registration text field. | `src/Views/PlayerRegistrationView.elm:17-24` | kept (K-5) |
| 2 | **Client** | Client (React `RegistrationView`, reducer, M-1) stores each keystroke and clears any previous error. | `src/Frontend.elm:47-48` | M-1 |
| 3 | **Actor** | Player clicks the "Join" button (or submits the form). | `src/Views/PlayerRegistrationView.elm:16`, `src/Views/PlayerRegistrationView.elm:25-28` | kept (K-5) |
| 4 | **Client** | Client trims the name; if non-empty it switches to the lobby view and sends `RegisterPlayer` over the typed WS (M-3). | `src/Frontend.elm:50-62` | M-3 |
| 5 | **Server** | Server checks for a duplicate name; if new, it prepends the name to the players list (K-3). | `src/Backend.elm:95-108` | kept (K-3) |
| 6 | **Server** | Server broadcasts `PlayerRegistrationUpdated` with the full roster to all connected clients including the actor (M-3). | `src/Backend.elm:111-113`, `src/Types.elm:68-70` | kept (K-4) · M-3 |
| 7 | **Client** | Every client in the lobby view refreshes its displayed player list from the broadcast (reducer, M-1). | `src/Frontend.elm:95-96`, `src/Views/PlayerLobbyView.elm:18-19` | kept (K-4) · M-1 |

**6. Alternative Flows (Extensions)**
* *(none in evidence)* — kept

**7. Exceptions (Error Flows)**
* **1a (at step 4, Client). Name is empty after trimming:** Client shows the error "Name cannot be empty." and does not contact the server. `src/Frontend.elm:56-57`, `src/Views/PlayerRegistrationView.elm:40-45` — kept (K-5)
* **2a (at step 5, Server). Name already exists in the lobby:** Server keeps the model unchanged and now returns a structured `RegistrationRejected { reason: "duplicate-name" }` (M-5) to the registering client; the client renders the reason in the registration view's error box (M-1) — closing the silent-drop gap (I-2). (was: silent rejection, no error surface. `src/Backend.elm:99-102`, `src/Frontend.elm:95-96`, `src/Views/PlayerLobbyView.elm:11-24`) — M-5
* **3a (at step 5, Server). Lobby already holds `playerLimit` (5) players:** Server rejects the addition and sends `LobbyIsFull` (now paired with `RegistrationRejected { reason: "lobby-full" }`, M-5) to the registering client; the client shows "Lobby is full." and offers a "Kill lobby" button (K-5). `src/Backend.elm:110-118`, `src/Types/Game.elm:43-45`, `src/Frontend.elm:107-115`, `src/Views/PlayerRegistrationView.elm:29-37` — kept (K-3) · M-5

**8. Special Requirements (Non-Functional Requirements)**
* **Capacity:** Lobby capacity is exactly 5 players (`playerLimit = 5`). `src/Types/Game.elm:43-45`, `src/Backend.elm:110` — kept (K-3)
* **Validation:** `PlayerName` is a plain string; server-side validation is duplicate rejection + the 5-cap, and the rejection reason is returned (M-5); there is no length/format validation. `src/Types/PlayerName.elm:4-5`, `src/Backend.elm:95-98` — kept (K-3) · M-5
* **Error surfacing:** Rejections are now observable: the registration view's error box receives real content for duplicate-name and full-lobby (M-5). (was: silent. `UseCaseModel.md:499`) — added (M-5)
* **Optimistic UI:** The client switches to the lobby view optimistically before the server accepts; a rejected client still renders the lobby. `src/Frontend.elm:60-61`, `src/Frontend.elm:165-166` — kept (K-5)

### UC-02: Kick a player from the lobby

**1. Brief Description**
A player in the lobby removes another player (or themselves) from the lobby list; the server
filters the name out and broadcasts `PlayerKicked` (M-3); the kicked client is reset to the
registration screen.

**2. Actors**
* **Primary:** Player (browser) (UC-A1)
* **Secondary:** Game server (UC-A2) (M-2)

**3. Pre-conditions**
* *Server/Client:* Server is in the lobby phase (`BePlayerRegistration`) and the acting client has the lobby view rendered. `src/Types.elm:11-14`, `src/Frontend.elm:165-166` — kept (K-3)

**4. Post-conditions**
* *System State:* The kicked name is removed and all clients received `PlayerKicked` with the updated roster. `src/Backend.elm:129-133`, `src/Types.elm:71-74` — kept (K-4)
* *System State:* The kicked client's frontend reset to the registration init state (name input cleared, no error). `src/Frontend.elm:98-100`, `src/Frontend.elm:34-41` — kept (K-5)

**5. Main Success Scenario (Happy Path)**

| # | Lane | Step | Code Reference | Modernization |
| :- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | **Actor** | A player clicks the red "kick" label next to a name in the lobby roster. | `src/Views/PlayerLobbyView.elm:30-37` | kept (K-5) |
| 2 | **Client** | Client (React `LobbyView`, M-1) sends `KickPlayer <name>` over the typed WS (M-3) with no local model change. | `src/Frontend.elm:64-65` | M-3 |
| 3 | **Server** | Server (M-2) filters the name out of the players list; the WebSocket session is bound to the acting registered player (M-4). | `src/Backend.elm:125-130` | kept (K-3) · M-4 |
| 4 | **Server** | Server broadcasts `PlayerKicked {kickedPlayer, players}` to all connected clients (M-3). | `src/Backend.elm:132`, `src/Types.elm:71-74` | kept (K-4) · M-3 |
| 5 | **Client** | Clients whose local `playerName` differs from `kickedPlayer` update their roster (reducer, M-1); the kicked client resets to the registration init state. | `src/Frontend.elm:98-105` | kept (K-5) |

**6. Alternative Flows (Extensions)**
* **1a (at step 1, Actor). Self-kick to leave the lobby:** A player clicks "kick" on their own name to leave the lobby: the roster control is rendered for every name including one's own, so self-kick is the only way a player exits the lobby on their own (K-3). `src/Views/PlayerLobbyView.elm:30-37`, `src/Frontend.elm:98-100` — kept (K-3)

**7. Exceptions (Error Flows)**
* **3a (at step 3, Server). Kick of an absent name is a no-op:** `KickPlayer` for a name not present in the lobby changes nothing — `List.filter` removes nothing, the model is unchanged and the unchanged roster is still broadcast. `src/Backend.elm:125-133` — kept (K-3)

**8. Special Requirements (Non-Functional Requirements)**
* **Session binding:** The WebSocket session is bound to the registered player (M-4); kicking semantics (any lobby name can be removed, self-kick included) are unchanged (K-3). (was: no server-side sender check. `src/Backend.elm:125-133`) — M-4
* **State discard:** Kicking discards all lobby client state for the kicked player (name input reset). `src/Frontend.elm:98-100`, `src/Frontend.elm:34-41` — kept (K-5)

### UC-03: Start a new game

**1. Brief Description**
Start button sends `InitializeGame`; the server (M-2) runs `initializeGame`, performs an
**in-process Fisher–Yates shuffle** of the draw stack (replaces the two Lamdera `Random`
re-entries, M-2), resolves the first playable tile (`getPlayableTileFromDrawstack`, K-1), and
broadcasts `GameInitialized` (M-3); every lobby client switches to the game view.

**2. Actors**
* **Primary:** Player (browser) (UC-A1)
* **Secondary:** Game server (UC-A2) (M-2)

**3. Pre-conditions**
* *Server:* Server is in the lobby phase (`BePlayerRegistration`) with a non-empty roster; `initializeGame` requires a non-empty players list. `src/Types.elm:11-14`, `src/Types/Game.elm:48-52` — kept (K-1)

**4. Post-conditions**
* *System State:* Server model is `BeGamePlayed` holding the new `Game` (all clients share it, K-4). `src/Backend.elm:146`, `src/Types.elm:15-17` — kept (K-4)
* *System State:* Every client switched to the game view and renders the board in `PlaceTileState` with the shuffled first tile to place. `src/Frontend.elm:134-141`, `src/Views/GameView.elm:28-29` — kept (K-5)

**5. Main Success Scenario (Happy Path)**

| # | Lane | Step | Code Reference | Modernization |
| :- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | **Actor** | A player in the lobby clicks the "Start" button. | `src/Views/PlayerLobbyView.elm:20-23` | kept (K-5) |
| 2 | **Client** | Client (React `LobbyView`, M-1) sends `InitializeGame` over the typed WS (M-3). | `src/Frontend.elm:67-68` | M-3 |
| 3 | **Server** | Server builds the new game via `initializeGame`: zeroed scores, 7 meeples per player (K-1), players array, `currentPlayer` 0, starting tile (0,0), `PlaceTileState`, full draw stack. | `src/Backend.elm:140-144`, `src/Types/Game.elm:53-73`, `src/Types/Game.elm:102-104` | kept (K-1) |
| 4 | **Server** | Server shuffles the draw stack **in-process (Fisher–Yates)** synchronously, with no platform re-entry. (was: `Random.List.shuffle` command + Lamdera re-entry. `src/Backend.elm:147`, `src/Types.elm:63`) | M-2 |
| 5 | **Server** | Server walks the shuffled stack with `getPlayableTileFromDrawstack`, skipping tiles that fit nowhere (in any rotation), and sets the first playable tile as `tileToPlace` (K-1). | `src/Backend.elm:46-54`, `src/Helpers/FrontendHelpers.elm:132-143` | kept (K-1) |
| 6 | **Server** | Server broadcasts `GameInitialized {game}` to all connected clients including the actor (M-3). | `src/Backend.elm:58`, `src/Types.elm:77-79` | kept (K-4) · M-3 |
| 7 | **Client** | Each client switches to the game board (React `GameBoard`: tile grid, sidebar with scores/meeples, drawn tile, Rotate button; M-1). | `src/Frontend.elm:134-141`, `src/Views/GameView.elm:21-27`, `src/Views/GameView.elm:641-749` | M-1 |

**6. Alternative Flows (Extensions)**
* **1a (at step 1, Actor). Rejected registrant can still start:** Any client holding the lobby view can start the game, including one whose registration was just rejected (the client switched to the lobby view optimistically). Start semantics are preserved (K-3); the server attributes the start to the acting session, whose WebSocket is bound to a registered name (M-4). `src/Views/PlayerLobbyView.elm:20-23`, `src/Backend.elm:140-144` — kept (K-3) · M-4

**7. Exceptions (Error Flows)**
* **5a (at step 5, Server). No placeable first tile (cannot happen with the fresh stack):** If no tile in the shuffled stack is placeable anywhere, `tileToPlace` falls back to tile 0 via `Maybe.withDefault` and the draw stack is emptied (K-1). `src/Backend.elm:46-54`, `src/Helpers/FrontendHelpers.elm:142-143` — kept (K-1)

**8. Special Requirements (Non-Functional Requirements)**
* **Meeple economy:** Each player starts with 7 meeples (K-1). `src/Types/Game.elm:61` — kept (K-1)
* **Tile set:** 71 tiles in the draw stack plus 1 starting tile (72 total) — the code-verified numbers, reused verbatim (K-1); resolves the legacy "74-tile" planner claim (A-41). `src/Types/Game.elm:120-147`, `src/Types/Game.elm:102-104` — kept (K-1)
* **Draw order:** Unplaceable tiles are consumed in shuffled order without re-shuffling; the stack is only re-shuffled after each meeple placement (now in-process, M-2). `src/Helpers/FrontendHelpers.elm:134-140`, `src/Backend.elm:177` — kept (K-1) · M-2

### UC-04: Place a tile on the board

**1. Brief Description**
The client highlights placeable coordinates for the drawn tile; click sends `PlaceTile
<coordinate>` (M-3); the server **revalidates the move server-side (M-4)** — tile placement
legality and turn ownership (WebSocket session bound to the acting player) — before
`placeTile` stamps new `SideId`s, inserts the tile, merges adjacent `SideId`s (tiles and
meeples, K-1), and sets `PlaceMeepleState` and `lastPlacedTile`; the new state is broadcast to
all clients (M-3). Invalid or out-of-turn moves are rejected with a structured `InvalidMove {
reason }` (M-5).

**2. Actors**
* **Primary:** Player (browser) (UC-A1)
* **Secondary:** Game server (UC-A2) (M-2)

**3. Pre-conditions**
* *Server:* Game state is `PlaceTileState`. `src/Types/GameState.elm:5`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:507` — kept (K-1)
* *Server/Client:* The acting client's WebSocket session is bound to the current player (`game.currentPlayer`) — now enforced server-side (M-4); the client also only renders placeable cells for the current player (UI hint, K-5). (was: enforced only in the client UI; the backend did not check the sender. `src/Views/GameView.elm:58-75`, `src/Backend.elm:160-168`) — M-4
* *Server:* `tileToPlace` is the drawn tile, guaranteed placeable in some rotation by the draw step. `src/Types/Game.elm:33`, `src/Helpers/FrontendHelpers.elm:132-143` — kept (K-1)

**4. Post-conditions**
* *System State:* The tile occupies the clicked coordinate and connected features across adjacent tiles share a single `SideId` (K-1). `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:347-362` — kept (K-1)
* *System State:* `GameState` is `PlaceMeepleState`, `lastPlacedTile` is the clicked coordinate, `nextSideId` advanced. `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:364-370`, `src/Types/GameState.elm:6` — kept (K-1)
* *System State:* All clients received `UpdateGameState` (M-3) and re-rendered. `src/Backend.elm:166-167`, `src/Frontend.elm:143-150` — kept (K-4) · M-3

**5. Main Success Scenario (Happy Path)**

| # | Lane | Step | Code Reference | Modernization |
| :- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | **Client** | Client (React `GameBoard`, M-1) computes placeable coordinates for the drawn tile in its current rotation (ported `tileCanBePlaced`, K-1) and renders them as highlighted clickable cells for the current player. | `src/Views/GameView.elm:58-75`, `src/Helpers/FrontendHelpers.elm:89-110`, `src/Helpers/FrontendHelpers.elm:48-84` | kept (K-1) · M-1 |
| 2 | **Actor** | The current-turn player clicks one of the highlighted cells. | `src/Views/GameView.elm:318-329` | kept (K-5) |
| 3 | **Client** | Client sends `PlaceTile <coordinate>` over the typed WS (M-3). | `src/Frontend.elm:76-77` | M-3 |
| 4 | **Server** | **Server revalidates the move (M-4):** it runs the ported `tileCanBePlaced` / `getCoordinatesToBePlacedOn` checks and verifies the acting session's player is `game.currentPlayer`; if the move is invalid or out-of-turn it returns a structured `InvalidMove { reason }` (M-5) and stops. | `UseCaseModel.md:284` | added (M-4) |
| 5 | **Server** | Server stamps the tile's side ids (offset by `nextSideId + 1`, leaving -1 sides untouched) via `updateSideIds` (K-1). | `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:326-329`, `src/Types/Tile.elm:62-81` | kept (K-1) |

No valid cell in the current rotation:** If the drawn tile's current rotation has no valid cell, `getCoordinatesToBePlacedOn` is empty, no cells are highlighted, and the player must rotate the tile (UC-05) to a placeable orientation before any click is possible (K-1). `src/Helpers/FrontendHelpers.elm:89-110`, `src/Views/GameView.elm:59-70`, `src/Views/GameView.elm:318-332` — kept (K-1)

Not the current player's turn:** A non-current player cannot place: the placeable overlay is rendered only for the current player (UI hint) AND the server rejects an out-of-turn `PlaceTile` with `InvalidMove { reason: "not-your-turn" }` (M-4, M-5). (was: client-side only. `src/Views/GameView.elm:58-75`) — M-4 · M-5

This closes the legacy gap where `placeTile` "does not check whether the move is valid" and a crafted message could overwrite an occupied cell (I-1). (was: client-trusted only. `src/Helpers/FrontendHelpers.elm:48-84`, `src/Views/GameView.elm:320-329`) — M-4
* **Feature tracking:** Feature connectivity is tracked purely by `SideId` rewriting across the grid (K-1). `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:326-362` — kept (K-1)

### UC-05: Rotate the drawn tile

**1. Brief Description**
The Rotate button sends `RotateTileLeft` (M-3); the server applies `rotateLeft` to
`tileToPlace` (sides shift counterclockwise, `rotation += 90` with a `modBy 360` overflow
guard, K-1) and **asserts the `isRotatedCorrectly` invariant at runtime (M-4)**; it then
broadcasts `UpdateGameState` (M-3); the client re-renders the sidebar tile with a CSS rotation
transform (M-1). A rotation message arriving in the wrong state now receives a structured
rejection (M-5) instead of a silent drop.

**2. Actors**
* **Primary:** Player (browser) (UC-A1)
* **Secondary:** Game server (UC-A2) (M-2)

**3. Pre-conditions**
* *Server:* Server is in the game phase (`BeGamePlayed`); the `RotateTileLeft` handler matches that state (M-4). `src/Types.elm:15-17`, `src/Backend.elm:150` — kept (K-1)

**4. Post-conditions**
* *System State:* `tileToPlace` is rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise and `isRotatedCorrectly` holds (K-1, M-4). `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:21-40` — kept (K-1)
* *System State:* All clients received `UpdateGameState` (M-3) and re-render the board and sidebar tile. `src/Backend.elm:156-157`, `src/Frontend.elm:143-150` — kept (K-4) · M-3

**5. Main Success Scenario (Happy Path)**

| 2 | **Client** | Client sends `RotateTileLeft` over the typed WS (M-3). | `src/Frontend.elm:70-71` | M-3 |
| 3 | **Server** | Server (M-2) applies `rotateLeft` to `tileToPlace`: north←east, west←north, south←west, east←south, and `rotation += 90` (with a `modBy 360` reset once ≥ 360000). | `src/Backend.elm:150-158`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:21-40` | kept (K-1) |
| 4 | **Server** | **Server asserts `isRotatedCorrectly` on the rotated tile (M-4)** — the ported rotation-invariant check now runs at runtime, not only in unit tests. | `UseCaseModel.md:504` | added (M-4) |
| 5 | **Server** | Server broadcasts `UpdateGameState {game}` to all connected clients including the actor (M-3). | `src/Backend.elm:156-157` | kept (K-4) · M-3 |
| 6 | **Client** | Each client re-renders the board and the sidebar tile image using a CSS transform of the negated rotation (M-1). | `src/Frontend.elm:143-150`, `src/Views/GameView.elm:727-734` | M-1 |

**6. Alternative Flows (Extensions)**
* **1a (at step 1, Actor). Rotate during the meeple phase:** Player clicks Rotate during `PlaceMeepleState`: the server still rotates the stored `tileToPlace`, but the sidebar shows only a placeholder image and the tile will be replaced by the next drawn tile after the meeple step anyway (K-1). `src/Views/GameView.elm:727-734`, `src/Backend.elm:150-158`, `src/Backend.elm:61-74` — kept (K-1)

**7. Exceptions (Error Flows)**

Rotation message in the lobby phase:** `RotateTileLeft` received while the server is in the lobby phase now receives a structured rejection `InvalidMove { reason: "wrong-state" }` (M-5) instead of a silent no-op drop. (was: matched no handler and was ignored. `src/Backend.elm:150`, `src/Backend.elm:185-186`) — added (M-5)

**8. Special Requirements (Non-Functional Requirements)**
* **Overflow guard:** Once `tile.rotation >= 360000` the rotation is normalized with `modBy 360` (K-1). `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:23-31` — kept (K-1)
* **Turn gating:** Rotation remains not turn-gated (the button is rendered for every player and the server applies `RotateTileLeft` from any client) — preserved (K-1); the rotation invariant itself is now server-asserted (M-4). `src/Views/GameView.elm:740-742`, `src/Backend.elm:150-158` — kept (K-1) · M-4

### UC-06: Place a meeple or skip

**1. Brief Description**
The client offers claimable positions on the last placed tile (or only Skip when the player
has no meeples left); click sends `PlaceMeeple <position>` (M-3); the server **revalidates
the move and turn ownership server-side (M-4)** before `placeMeeple` inserts the meeple by
`SideId` (K-1), scores finished features (UC-07, K-1), and advances the turn to
`PlaceTileState`; the server then re-shuffles the draw stack in-process (M-2) and draws the
next placeable tile (or finishes the game). Invalid/out-of-turn moves are rejected with
`InvalidMove { reason }` (M-5).

**2. Actors**
* **Primary:** Player (browser) (UC-A1)
* **Secondary:** Game server (UC-A2) (M-2)

**3. Pre-conditions**
* *Server:* Game state is `PlaceMeepleState` (set by `placeTile` after every tile placement). `src/Types/GameState.elm:6`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:367` — kept (K-1)
* *Server/Client:* The acting client's WebSocket session is bound to the current player — now enforced server-side (M-4); the client renders the overlay for the current player only (UI hint). (was: enforced only in the client UI; the backend attributed the meeple to `game.currentPlayer` regardless of the sender. `src/Views/GameView.elm:121-142`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:386-391`) — M-4

**4. Post-conditions**
* *System State:* `currentPlayer` advanced (wrap-around) and `gameState` is `PlaceTileState` (K-1). `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:502-508`, `src/Types/Game.elm:78-84` — kept (K-1)
* *System State:* Finished features on the last placed tile are scored to their majority owners, their `SideId`s removed from the meeples dict, and meeples returned (K-1). `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:418-500` — kept (K-1)
* *System State:* A new `tileToPlace` is drawn from the re-shuffled (in-process, M-2) stack (or the game is finished); all clients received the new state (M-3). `src/Backend.elm:177`, `src/Backend.elm:61-84`, `src/Frontend.elm:143-150` — kept (K-1) · M-2 · M-3

**5. Main Success Scenario (Happy Path)**

| # | Lane | Step | Code Reference | Modernization |
| :- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | **Client** | Client (React `GameBoard`, M-1) computes claimable positions on the last placed tile (ported helpers, K-1): all sides whose `SideId` has no meeple and is not -1, plus `Center` when the tile has a cloister; offered only while the player still has meeples, otherwise only Skip. | `src/Views/GameView.elm:121-142`, `src/Helpers/FrontendHelpers.elm:27-43`, `src/Views/GameView.elm:524-536` | kept (K-1) · M-1 |
| 2 | **Actor** | The current-turn player clicks one of the position circles. | `src/Views/GameView.elm:533` | kept (K-5) |
| 3 | **Client** | Client sends `PlaceMeeple <position>` over the typed WS (M-3). | `src/Frontend.elm:79-80` | M-3 |
| 4 | **Server** | **Server revalidates the move (M-4):** verifies the position is claimable (unoccupied, `SideId /= -1`) and the acting session's player is `game.currentPlayer`; invalid/out-of-turn → `InvalidMove { reason }` (M-5) and stop. | `UseCaseModel.md:376` | added (M-4) |
| 5 | **Server** | Server constructs the meeple (owner = `currentPlayer`, coordinates = `lastPlacedTile`) and inserts it under the matching `SideId` (Center → cloister `SideId`, K-1). | `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:383-413`, `src/Types/Meeple.elm:17-23` | kept (K-1) |
| 6 | **Server** | Server scores finished features (UC-07, K-1): counts each, doubles cities with score > 2, appends finished-cloister scores. | `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:418-438`, `src/Types/Tile.elm:42-45`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:193-203`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:170-189` | kept (K-1) |

Skip meeple placement:** Player clicks the "Skip Meeple placement" button: `Skip` is sent; `placeMeeple` leaves the meeples dictionary unchanged for `Skip`, skips the -1 meeple-count decrement, and otherwise advances the turn and draws exactly like the main flow (K-1). `src/Views/GameView.elm:382-395`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:415-416`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:493-500` — kept (K-1)
* **1b (at step 1, Client). No meeples left:** The player has no meeples left (`playerMeeples == 0`): only `[Skip]` is offered (K-1). `src/Helpers/FrontendHelpers.elm:29-31`, `src/Helpers/FrontendHelpers.elm:42-43` — kept (K-1)

(was: backend did not check. `src/Helpers/FrontendHelpers.elm:32-40`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:400-413`) — M-4 · M-5
* **9a (at step 9, Server). No placeable tile remains:** No placeable tile remains in the (re-shuffled) draw stack: the server calls `finishGame`, which scores all remaining features and cloisters, empties the meeples dict, and sets `FinishedState`; the finished game is broadcast (UC-07, K-1). `src/Backend.elm:76-84`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:511-556` — kept (K-1)

**8. Special Requirements (Non-Functional Requirements)**
* **Meeple economy:** Players start with 7 meeples (K-1); the Skip option is always available in the UI (K-5). `src/Types/Game.elm:61`, `src/Views/GameView.elm:382-395` — kept (K-1)
* **Turn check (now server-side):** The server `PlaceMeeple` handler revalidates turn ownership via the session→player binding (M-4); the meeple's owner is `game.currentPlayer`. (was: no turn check in the backend. `src/Backend.elm:170-178`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:386-391`) — M-4 (closes I-1)
* **Shuffle rule:** The draw stack is re-shuffled after every meeple placement (Skip included), now in-process (M-2), per the readme rule. `src/Backend.elm:177`, `readme.md:60-61` — kept (K-1) · M-2

### UC-07: Score a completed feature by majority

**1. Brief Description**
System-internal scoring, triggered by a player's meeple placement/skip (UC-06, steps 5–7) or
by `finishGame` at game end (K-1): when a feature touched by the last placed tile is finished
(or at game end), its size in tiles is awarded to the player(s) with the most meeples on it;
ties award the full score to every tied player. This is a derived use case — it has no own
client→server message (K-6); the actor is the acting player of UC-06 (A-44).

**2. Actors**
* **Primary:** Player (browser) (UC-A1) — the acting player of UC-06 whose meeple step (or skip) triggers mid-game scoring; the player does not act directly on this use case (A-44).
* **Secondary:** Game server (UC-A2) (M-2) — fans the resulting `UpdateGameState` out to all clients (M-3).

**3. Pre-conditions**
* *Server:* A `SideId` is under evaluation: either a side/cloister of the last placed tile after a meeple step (mid-game), or any `SideId` still holding meeples at game end. `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:418-422`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:514-518` — kept (K-1)

**4. Post-conditions**
* *System State:* The majority owner(s)' totals in `playerScores` are increased by the feature score (mid-game) or by all remaining feature/cloister scores (game end) (K-1). `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:444-464`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:529-550` — kept (K-1)
* *System State:* Mid-game: the scored `SideId`s are removed from the meeples dict and their meeples returned to owners. Game end: the meeples dict is emptied and `gameState` is `FinishedState` (K-1). `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:440-442`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:551-556` — kept (K-1)

**5. Main Success Scenario (Happy Path)**

| # | Lane | Step | Code Reference | Modernization |
| :- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | **Server** | After the meeple step, server collects the unique `SideId`s of the last placed tile (edges plus cloister, -1 excluded) via `getTileSideIds` (K-1). | `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:418-422`, `src/Types/Tile.elm:42-57` | kept (K-1) |
| 2 | **Server** | Server keeps only the finished `SideId`s: for every tile of the feature, each side carrying the `SideId` must have a placed neighbour tile (`isFeatureFinished`, K-1). | `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:422`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:193-203` | kept (K-1) |
| 3 | **Server** | Server counts the feature's size as the number of grid tiles sharing the `SideId` (`countFeature`) and doubles the score when it is a city with score > 2 (completed before the game ends, K-1). | `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:423-436`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:170-189` | kept (K-1) |
| 4 | **Server** | Server appends scores for cloisters completed around the last placed tile: a cloister scoring 9 when its 3×3 neighbourhood is complete (K-1). | `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:437-438`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:230-251`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:211-224` | kept (K-1) |
| 5 | **Server** | Server determines the owner(s) via `getFeatureOwners`: meeples under the `SideId` are counted per player index and every player reaching the maximum count is kept (ties share, K-1). | `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:449-451`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:256-290` | kept (K-1) |
| 6 | **Server** | Server adds the feature score to each owner's total in `playerScores` (one entry per tied owner, K-1). | `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:444-464` | kept (K-1) |
| 7 | **Server** | Server returns the feature's meeples to their owners' pools (+1 each) and removes the scored `SideId`s from the meeples dict (K-1); the resulting full state is broadcast to all clients (M-3). | `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:440-442`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:470-492` | kept (K-1) · M-3 |

**6. Alternative Flows (Extensions)**
* **1a (at step 1, Server). Game-end variant:** When the draw stack is exhausted, `finishGame` scores every remaining feature `SideId` (`countFeature`) and every cloister (`countCloister`) with no 2× city bonus, sets meeples to empty and `gameState` to `FinishedState`, and the result is broadcast as `UpdateGameState` (M-3) (K-1). `src/Backend.elm:76-84`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:511-556`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:211-224` — kept (K-1) · M-3
* **5a (at step 5, Server). Tie on the maximum meeple count:** `getFeatureOwners` returns all tied players, so each tied player receives the full feature score (the score is not divided, K-1). `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:288-290`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:446-451` — kept (K-1)

**7. Exceptions (Error Flows)**
* **2a (at step 2, Server). Unfinished features are not scored:** The `SideId` is filtered out by `isFeatureFinished` and its meeples remain on the board for a later turn (K-1). `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:422`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:193-203` — kept (K-1)
* **5b (at step 5, Server). Finished feature with no meeples scores nobody:** `getFeatureOwners` yields an empty owner list and no score entry is produced (K-1). `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:256-264`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:288-290` — kept (K-1)

**8. Special Requirements (Non-Functional Requirements)**
* **2× city bonus:** Applies only to mid-game completion with score strictly greater than 2; `finishGame` applies no bonus (K-1). `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:430-436`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:511-556` — kept (K-1)
* **Cloister value:** A completed cloister always scores 9 tiles (K-1). `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:250-251`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:211-224` — kept (K-1)
* **Tie rule:** Tied majorities each receive the full score rather than splitting it (K-1). `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:288-290` — kept (K-1)

**1. Brief Description**
A player whose browser was disconnected (or a fresh browser) registers a name while the
server already holds a running game; the server returns the model unchanged, sends
`JoinedGame {game}` to that client only (M-3), and the client switches from the lobby view to
the shared game view (K-4).

**2. Actors**
* **Primary:** Player (browser) (UC-A1)
* **Secondary:** Game server (UC-A2) (M-2)

**3. Pre-conditions**
* *Server:* Server is in the game phase (`BeGamePlayed`) — a game was started by the lobby. `src/Types.elm:15-17`, `src/Backend.elm:140-148` — kept (K-4)

**4. Post-conditions**
* *System State:* The reconnecting client renders the shared game (K-4). `src/Frontend.elm:125-132` — kept (K-4)
* *System State:* The server model is unchanged: the re-entered name is **NOT** added to the game's player roster (K-4). `src/Backend.elm:120-123`, `src/Types/Game.elm:28-40` — kept (K-4)

**5. Main Success Scenario (Happy Path)**

| # | Lane | Step | Code Reference | Modernization |
| :- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | **Actor** | The (reconnecting) player enters a name in the registration view and clicks "Join". | `src/Views/PlayerRegistrationView.elm:17-28`, `src/Frontend.elm:50-57` | kept (K-5) |
| 2 | **Client** | Client (React, M-1) switches to the lobby view and sends `RegisterPlayer <name>` over the typed WS (M-3). | `src/Frontend.elm:60-62` | M-3 |
| 3 | **Server** | Server, being in `BeGamePlayed`, returns the model unchanged and sends `JoinedGame {game}` to that client only (M-3, K-4). | `src/Backend.elm:120-123` | kept (K-4) · M-3 |
| 4 | **Client** | Client switches from the lobby view to the game view with the current shared game and renders the live board (M-1). | `src/Frontend.elm:125-132`, `src/Views/GameView.elm:21-27` | M-1 |

**6. Alternative Flows (Extensions)**
* **2a (at step 2, Server). Still in the lobby phase:** If the server is still in the lobby phase, `RegisterPlayer` is handled as a normal registration (UC-01) instead; a freshly connected client also receives the current roster via the connection lifecycle (M-2) (K-4). `src/Backend.elm:93-118`, `src/Backend.elm:40-42`, `src/Backend.elm:189-191` — kept (K-4) · M-2

**7. Exceptions (Error Flows)**
* **3a (at step 3, Server). Re-entered name is not a game player:** The re-entered name is not part of the game roster: scores and meeple pools are keyed by the original player names, so the reconnected client sees the game under its local display name but the server never associates it with a game player (K-4). `src/Backend.elm:120-123`, `src/Types/Game.elm:29-31`, `src/Frontend.elm:125-132` — kept (K-4)
* **3b (at step 3, Server). Session bound on reconnection:** On reconnection the WebSocket session is bound to the registered name (M-4); the client still cannot act on the game until its name matches `game.currentPlayer` (turn check now server-enforced, M-4). (was: no identity check on reconnection. `src/Backend.elm:120-123`) — M-4

**8. Special Requirements (Non-Functional Requirements)**
* **Documented behaviour:** "If somebody got disconnected, they can re-enter their name and they can continue playing." `readme.md:121-123` — kept (K-4)
* **Passive reconnection:** The client cannot act on the game until its name matches `game.currentPlayer` — now enforced server-side (M-4) as well as client-side (K-5). `src/Views/GameView.elm:58-75`, `src/Views/GameView.elm:121-142` — kept (K-4) · M-4

Every scoped plan decision applied in this document, with where it lands and the legacy evidence it transforms; the kept elements (K-n) are listed in the same table.

| Ref | Decision | Applied to | Legacy evidence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| M-1 | Rewrite the Elm browser frontend as a TypeScript SPA (React 19, Vite 7, CSS modules; `RegistrationView`/`LobbyView`/`GameBoard`) | §2.1, all UC client lanes, §6.2 | `elm.json:4-13`, `src/Frontend.elm:17-31`, `src/Views/GameView.elm:1` |
| M-2 | Rewrite the Elm/Lamdera backend as a Node.js 24 + `ws` 8.x server owning one authoritative in-memory state; in-process Fisher–Yates shuffle; structured logging (no `Debug.log`) | §2.2 (game-server actor), UC-03/UC-06 shuffle, UC-08 connection lifecycle | `elm.json:17-18`, `src/Backend.elm:18-25`, `src/Backend.elm:147` |
| M-3 | Typed WebSocket JSON protocol: 8 client→server + 8 legacy server→client discriminated unions (10 server→client incl. the two M-5 additions), zod-validated server-side, full-state broadcast to every client incl. the actor; typed WS client. Plan note: the plan's M-3 "9 server→client" is a plan-level count error superseded by the code-verified 8 (`src/Types.elm:67-86`). | §2 boundary table, all UC server/client lanes | `src/Types.elm:50-58`, `src/Types.elm:67-86`, `src/Backend.elm:6` |
| M-4 | Server-side revalidation of move legality + turn ownership (WebSocket session bound to the registered player); `isRotatedCorrectly` becomes a runtime invariant on the rotation path | UC-04 step 4, UC-05 step 4, UC-06 step 4, UC-08 3b | `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:311-314`, `src/Backend.elm:150-183`, `UseCaseModel.md:284` |
| M-5 | Structured error/rejection payloads (`RegistrationRejected { reason }`, `InvalidMove { reason }`; duplicate name, full lobby, invalid move, out-of-turn) with explicit client-side display | §2 boundary (added rows), UC-01 2a/3a, UC-04 2a/4a, UC-05 2a, UC-06 1a | `UseCaseModel.md:499`, `Specification.md:151`, `src/Backend.elm:99-102` |
| K-1 | Rule core kept (tile draw + placement legality, `SideId` merging, meeple placement/return, majority-with-tie scoring, 2× city bonus only for completed cities >2 tiles, cloister scoring, flat 7-meeples economy, turn machine, game ends when no tile placeable, unplaceable tiles skipped) | §1.3, UC-03/UC-04/UC-05/UC-06/UC-07 | `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:323-370`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:256-290` |
| K-3 | Player identity semantics (name-only, unique non-empty, 5-player lobby cap, kick/kill-lobby affordances, single `PLAYER` role) | §2.1, UC-01/UC-02/UC-08 | `src/Backend.elm:93-118`, `src/Backend.elm:125-133` |
| K-4 | Single shared authoritative game state (one in-memory lobby/game model, at most one concurrent game, full-state broadcast, non-acting clients read-only, reconnect = re-register) | §2, UC-01/UC-03/UC-06/UC-07/UC-08 | `src/Backend.elm:14-15`, `src/Backend.elm:120-123` |
| K-5 | Three-view UX flow and controls (registration, lobby, game board; debug SideId overlay non-interactive) | §2.1, §6.2, all client lanes | `src/Views/GameView.elm:21-749`, `src/Views/PlayerLobbyView.elm:11-37` |
| K-6 | Message-surface semantics (8 client→server, 8 legacy server→client messages, 10 incl. the two M-5 additions; keep payloads and state-gating). Plan note: the plan's K-6 "9 server→client" is a plan-level count error superseded by the code-verified 8 (`src/Types.elm:67-86`). | §2 boundary table, §5 | `src/Types.elm:50-58`, `src/Types.elm:67-86` |

**Replaced elements (no longer present under a decision — noted here, not deleted):**
* **Lamdera platform (secondary actor UC-A2)** → replaced by **M-2** (the Node.js 24 + `ws` 8.x game server owning the authoritative state).
* **`ToBackend`/`ToFrontend` ADT transport** → replaced by **M-3** (typed WebSocket JSON discriminated unions, zod-validated).
* **Lamdera `Random` shuffle re-entry** → replaced by **M-2** (in-process Fisher–Yates shuffle, no platform round-trip).

## Resolved Assumptions & Issues

Every scoped assumption (A-n) and issue (I-n) from `modernization-plan.json`, with terminal status and where in this document the resolution is visible. Statuses come from the plan; the quoted markers are the source text as it stood.

| Ref | Source | Original marker | Status | Resolution / Reason |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| A-36 | UseCaseModel.md | "Client-only validation ... ALL move/turn validation is client-side only" (`UseCaseModel.md:496`) | resolved | M-4 adds server-side revalidation (session→player binding + ported pure-domain checks), so this code fact no longer holds; visible in UC-04 step 4, UC-05 step 4, UC-06 step 4. The underlying defect is tracked as I-1. |
| A-37 | UseCaseModel.md | "No turn timers ... UNVERIFIED whether the Lamdera host layer imposes any timeout" (`UseCaseModel.md:497`) | deferred | Not requested by the directive; the modernized server (M-2) has no timer either and legacy stall behaviour is preserved. |
| A-38 | UseCaseModel.md | "Readme discrepancy — meeple count: The readme says '6 meeples + 1 on the score track' (readme.md:50) while the code initializes 7 meeples per player with no separate score-track meeple" (`UseCaseModel.md:498`) | accepted | The code value (flat 7 meeples, no score track) is the enforced behaviour and is preserved (K-1); visible in UC-03/UC-06 special requirements. |
| A-39 | UseCaseModel.md | "Terminate Game is out of scope: the Terminate Game feature exists ... but is not among the 8 planned use cases and was not modeled as a UC" (`UseCaseModel.md:500`) | accepted | The feature is kept in the rewrite (K-5/K-6); whether it becomes a 9th UC is a writer choice — semantics are unchanged either way; kept out of scope here (8 UCs). |
| A-40 | UseCaseModel.md | "No host/admin role: no host/admin role exists in code; ... a single PLAYER role was modeled" (`UseCaseModel.md:501`) | accepted | Domain fact preserved by the rewrite (K-3); no role-system directive; single `PLAYER` role in §2.1. |
| A-41 | UseCaseModel.md | "Tile-set count: planner scope note said '74-tile set'; the code builds a 71-tile draw stack plus 1 starting tile" (`UseCaseModel.md:502`) | resolved | Code-verified (71-tile draw stack + 1 starting tile = 72); the modernized data layer reuses the code-verified 71+1 numbers verbatim; visible in UC-03 special requirements. |
| A-42 | UseCaseModel.md | "Debug-mode claim: readme.md:129 claims tiles/meeples cannot be placed while debug mode is on; the code does not block placement" (`UseCaseModel.md:503`) | accepted | The enforced behaviour (placement active during debug mode) is preserved (K-5); the debug overlay stays a non-interactive visual layer (`pointer-events: none`). |
| A-43 | UseCaseModel.md | "Rotation invariant unenforced at runtime: isRotatedCorrectly is exercised only by unit tests" (`UseCaseModel.md:504`) | resolved | M-4 makes the ported check a server-side runtime invariant on the rotation path (UC-05 step 4); the pinned unit tests are ported to the modern test suite. |
| A-44 | UseCaseModel.md | "UC-07 is a derived use case: it has no own ToBackend entry; it is triggered by UC-06 (steps 4–6) or by draw-stack exhaustion ... not a direct player action on scoring" (`UseCaseModel.md:505`) | accepted | Modelling fact of the domain — scoring has no own message (K-6); UC-07 is kept derived in this document. |
| I-1 | Specification.md | "Client-trusted rules — ... so a tampered client could place invalid moves or play out of turn" (`Specification.md:111`) | resolved | M-4 revalidates move legality and turn ownership server-side (session bound to player, ported pure-domain checks); M-5 returns structured rejections for rejected moves; visible in UC-04/UC-05/UC-06. |
| I-2 | Specification.md | "there are no error payloads — a duplicate registration name is rejected silently (unchanged player list re-sent)" (`Specification.md:151`) | resolved | M-5 adds structured error/rejection payloads (`RegistrationRejected`, `InvalidMove`; duplicate name, full lobby, invalid move, out-of-turn) with explicit client-side display; visible in the §2 boundary and UC-01. |
